tagline.text: Hot springs and a walk past seven waterfalls at the foot of Mount Kanlaon

image.credit: Austin Rex Lobaton / CC BY-SA 4.0 / Wikimedia Commons

items.credit: Elmer B. Domingo / CC BY-SA 3.0 / Wikimedia Commons

children.text: A century-old mountain resort in the forest on the western slopes of Mount Kanlaon, about an hour east of Bacolod. Soak in sulfur hot springs, walk past the seven waterfalls strung along the valley, and watch a bat colony blanket the sky at dusk.
Mambukal Resort is a provincial-government-run mountain retreat in Murcia, Negros Occidental. Set about
east of the provincial capital Bacolod, at the foot of Mount Kanlaon at roughly
elevation, its air is cooler and its forest denser than the city. The entire
23.6-hectare
resort sits inside Mount Kanlaon Natural Park, making it a "park in the mountains" where hot springs, waterfalls, ponds, and forest trails all come together.
Mambukal's history goes back a century. The provincial government designated it a weekend retreat (a hill station) in
, and in

the Ishiwata Bathhouse, designed by Japanese architect Kokichi Paul Ishiwata, was built as the first permanent structure. The white bathhouse, lined with arched columns, pipes hot spring water into tiled tubs; long neglected, it has since been restored to its original look and remains open for bathing today. A Republic Act on
confirmed provincial-government management, and every
June
, the Mudpack Festival marks the date with dancers covered head to toe in mud.

The resort's signature feature is a chain of seven waterfalls strung one after another along the valley. A forest trail inside the resort leads up to the first through sixth falls, while the seventh and final one lies beyond the resort boundary, requiring a further walk toward the mountain village. Heated by volcanic geothermal activity, the hot springs reach up to around
, and you can soak away the fatigue of hiking in a sulfur-scented open-air pool or a Japanese-style bath.

The forest is home to rare animals such as large fruit bats like the golden-crowned flying fox, the Visayan warty pig, and the Negros bleeding-heart pigeon, and at dusk thousands of bats take flight all at once, filling the sky. With a zipline, canopy walk, boats, and a butterfly garden as well, it suits family outings with kids and travelers wanting to add a day of nature to a Bacolod-Silay trip.
It's about
1 hour
along a marked trail inside the resort to the sixth falls, and another
30 minutes
beyond that to the seventh. Each waterfall differs in height and shape, so there's fun in counting them off as you climb.
You can dip into cool mountain water in the pools below the sixth and seventh falls. Only go in when the current isn't strong, and follow your guide's instructions.
Soak in hot spring water piped into the white arched building built in
. Bathing here while sensing nearly a century of history is an experience unique to Mambukal.

blocks.title: Sulfur Open-Air Pool and Japanese Bath

children.text: The sulfur hot spring pool and the Japanese-style outdoor bath (rotenburo) in the forest are great to visit after trekking. Usage fees are separate from the entrance fee.
As the sun sets, thousands of fruit bats take off all at once from the forest above the resort to search for food. Look up at the sky from the pond around

blocks.title: Slide for Life and the Canopy Walk

children.text: The Slide for Life zipline crossing the valley on a cable, and the Canopy Walk hanging bridge up in the trees, are especially popular with kids and teens.
Rent a small boat on the pond at the heart of the resort, and get an up-close look at Negros butterflies at the butterfly garden.
In
August 2026

, five endangered Visayan spotted deer were moved from the Talarak Foundation conservation center to an enclosure inside the resort. It is preparing to open them to the public so visitors can see them up close along a trail, so check on-site whether viewing is available.

From Manila to Bacolod-Silay Airport (BCD) takes about
1 hour 10 minutes
, and from Cebu about
40 minutes
. From the airport to downtown Bacolod is about
30–40 minutes
by car, and going straight from the airport to Mambukal takes about
1 hour–1 hour 20 minutes
Fast craft between Iloilo City and Bacolod run several times a day, taking about
1 hour–1 hour 15 minutes
, for around
one-way. It pairs well with a Panay Island trip.
Minibuses and jeepneys run from a terminal near the Libertad public market in Bacolod, via Murcia, to Mambukal. It takes about
1 hour–1 hour 30 minutes
, for around
one-way.
Service thins out in the late afternoon, so check the return schedule as soon as you arrive.
From downtown Bacolod by taxi or Grab takes about
45 minutes–1 hour
, for around
one-way. Cars are hard to find for the return trip, so it's better to agree on a waiting fee with the driver or book a round trip.
Drive east from Bacolod along the road toward Murcia, about
45 minutes–1 hour
. There's parking at the resort entrance, with a separate vehicle entrance fee.
Western Negros has its dry season from
December to May
December–February
in particular sees morning and evening temperatures at Mambukal's higher elevation drop to around
, the best time for enjoying the hot springs, and the trekking paths dry out and are easy to walk.
March–May
brings midday heat around
in Bacolod, but Mambukal's shaded forest serves as a cool escape. Toward the end of the dry season, though, the waterfalls carry less water.
June–November
is the rainy season, when the waterfalls carry the most water, but forest trails get slippery and access to the falls may be restricted after heavy rain. Typhoons most often cross the Visayas during
September–December
. The Mudpack Festival takes place in
June
, and Bacolod's MassKara Festival in
October
, making a trip combining both popular — but book accommodation ahead for these periods. Weekdays are quiet, while weekends and school breaks bring crowds of families.

Inside Mambukal Resort are provincial-government-run rooms, cottages, villas, and a convention hotel. Double rooms start at about
a night, family cottages and villas run about

, and there are budget lodgings and a campground too. Staying overnight in the forest lets you take your time with the dusk bat colony, a night soak, and an early-morning waterfall trek. Rooms fill up fast on weekends and holidays, so check with the resort's booking office in advance. If you want a hotel with more amenities, stay in downtown Bacolod and visit as a day trip.
In
September 2026

, three luxury lake-view villas (up to 5 people each) with private hot spring baths, cold plunge pools, and bonfire gardens are slated to open, and the family cottages have also been refurbished. Ask the resort's reservation desk about villa rates and booking.
Inside the resort are a food court (4 restaurants) that opened in
, a garden cafe that opened in

, and a snack shop, where you can buy Filipino home cooking, seafood, and simple food, and many local families rent a hut (kubo) and eat packed lunches. Once back in Bacolod, be sure to try chicken inasal, chicken grilled over charcoal. Manokan Country, formerly the inasal stall street, closed in
, but the famous inasal restaurants operate elsewhere in the city, and piaya, a flat pastry made with Negros sugar, makes a good gift.

Set off early in the morning if you're going all the way to the seventh falls. The trail up to the sixth is well marked, but the seventh lies on a mountain path outside the resort, so it's safer to go with a guide.
The waterfall trail has been reopening section by section after repair work in
. When you arrive, first check at the ticket office how far the falls are open and whether a guide is required.
Non-slip sandals or aqua shoes are good for trekking, and bring a swimsuit, towel, and change of clothes.
Soaking before trekking will leave you feeling sluggish. Do the waterfall trek first and save the hot spring for last.
The bats take off over a short window at dusk. Wait in an open spot by the pond, and avoid using flash photography.
Facilities inside the resort each charge their own fee, so bring plenty of cash. There's no ATM nearby, or it's far from the resort.
Free golf carts run inside the resort, so if you're with seniors, people with mobility difficulties, or children, you can get around the large resort comfortably.
The elevation keeps evenings cool. If staying overnight, bring a light jacket.
Combining this with sightseeing in Bacolod and Silay rounds out a full 2-day, 1-night Negros trip.
Mambukal sits on the western slopes of Mount Kanlaon, an active volcano. Mount Kanlaon has been erupting intermittently since
, and climbing to the summit is banned; ashfall is possible nearby during eruptions. Before visiting, check the latest PHIVOLCS alert level and whether the resort is open.
When the alert level rose to Level 3 after the
December 2024
eruption, the Department of Tourism halted trekking, swimming, and day tours in ashfall-affected areas such as Murcia, and Mambukal also temporarily closed. As of
September 2026
the alert is Level 2 (entry to the
4km
-radius Permanent Danger Zone around the crater is banned), and the same measures could be imposed if the alert rises again.
The rocks around the waterfalls are very slippery with moss. Don't climb onto the top of a waterfall or the edge of a rock for photos.
Heavy rain can cause the stream to rise suddenly. If the water turns muddy or the level rises, get out of the water immediately.
Some hot spring water runs quite hot, so don't stay in too long if you have high blood pressure or a heart condition, or after drinking. Children should be closely supervised.
Don't feed or touch the bats or other wildlife. The forest may have mosquitoes and leeches, so insect repellent is a good idea.
Entrance fees, facility charges, and operating hours can change based on provincial policy, so check the latest notices.
